q: When a battery is connected to an external circuit, the terminal voltage of a battery is ______ [2025]
e: Terminal voltage of a discharging battery connected to an external circuit is given by V = E - Ir.

q: There are ______ joule in one kilowatt hour (1 kWh). [2024]
Which of the following statements is correct regarding most sources of electromotive force (EMF)? [2024]
a: EMF sources have no internal resistance.
EMF sources have no internal capacitance.
e: Most real EMF sources such as batteries possess internal resistance.

q: The heating element of an electric iron is controlled by a ______ that switches the current on and off to maintain the selected temperature. [2024]
e: A thermostat controls the heating element by switching current on and off.

q: ______ is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. [2025]
e: Electrical power is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is transferred.

q: In an electric generator, ______ energy is converted into electrical energy. [2026]
e: An electric generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

q: The unit of electrical power P is ______. [2025]
e: The standard unit of electrical power is watt (W).

q: On which factor does the heat produced in a current carrying conductor depend? [2024]
e: According to Joule's Law, heat produced in a conductor depends directly on current.

q: In charging battery, the potential difference between the terminals is ______. [2024]
e: When charging a battery, the applied terminal potential difference is given by E + Ir.

q: If two batteries having equal emfs and equal internal resistances are connected in parallel, what is resultant internal resistance of combination? [2024]
e: Two equal internal resistances r connected in parallel give an equivalent resistance of r / 2.

q: What component of an electric iron is responsible for maintaining the selected temperature by switching the current on and off? [2025]
e: A thermostat is responsible for switching current on and off to maintain temperature.

q: A device consuming 2kW of power for 3 hours would use electrical energy of ______. [2025]
e: Electrical energy = Power × Time = 2 kW × 3 h = 6 kWh.

q: What is electrical energy typically measured in? [2025]
e: Electrical energy is typically measured in joules (J) or kilowatt-hours.

q: At a temperature of ______, the tungsten filament emits white light. [2025]
e: Tungsten filament emits white light when heated to around 1800°C.

q: The amount of heat produced in a resistor due to a current flowing through it is ______ to the square of the current. [2025]
e: By Joule's law (H = I²Rt / J), heat generated is directly proportional to the square of current.

q: Which quantity determines the rate at which electrical energy is delivered by a current. [2025]
e: Electrical power determines the rate at which electrical energy is delivered.

q: The electromotive force (emf) of a source is defined as: [2025]
a: The potential difference across the terminals when no current flows,
The potential difference when the current is flowing,
The energy dissipated per unit charge.
e: EMF is defined as the potential difference across source terminals in an open circuit.

q: What is the SI unit of electrical power? [2025]
e: The SI unit of electrical power is Watt.

q: If an electric stove of 1200 W is connected to a 220 V mains line, the current flowing through it is ______. [2026]
e: Current I = P / V = 1200 W / 220 V ≈ 5.45 A.

q: When two batteries are connected in parallel, the voltage across each battery is: [2025]
a: The sum of the individual voltages
Equal to the voltage of one of the batteries
e: In parallel connections, terminal voltage across each parallel branch remains equal.

q: What is the commercial unit of electrical energy? [2025]
e: The commercial unit of electrical energy is kilowatt-hour (kWh).

q: Which of the following metals cannot be used as fuse wire? [2025]
e: Iron is unsuitable for fuse wire due to its high melting point and oxidation properties.

q: On which off the following effects of electric current a fuse operates? [2025]
e: Fuses operate based on the heating effect of electric current.

q: Which of the following equations is the total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit? [2025]
e: Total work done round complete circuit equals external plus internal work (IR + Ir).

q: On which factor does the heat produced in a current carrying conductor depend? [2025]
e: Heat generated in a conductor depends on current flowing through it.

q: Mica is a good electrical ______ and can withstand very high temperature. [2025]
e: Mica is an excellent electrical insulator capable of withstanding extreme heat.

q: Which quantity determines the rate at which electrical energy is delivered by a current? [2025]
e: Electrical power is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is delivered.

q: The heating element of an electric iron is controlled by a ______ to maintain the selected temperature. [2025]
e: A thermostat regulates the heating element temperature.

q: In charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to ______. [2025]
e: During charging, terminal potential difference equals E + Ir.

q: There are ______ joules in one kilowatt hour. [2025]
e: 1 kWh equals 3.6 × 10⁶ joules.

q: An electric stove has an electrical power ranging from 600 W to ______. [2025]
e: Power consumption of a standard electric stove ranges from 600 W to 2000 W.

q: The ______ energy is transformed into electrical energy by a battery. [2025]
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

q: A refrigerator has an electrical power ranging from 100 W to ______. [2026]
e: Electrical power rating of a refrigerator typically ranges from 100 W to 250 W.

q: The resultant emf of two batteries in ______ is the difference between the individuals emfs. [2026]
e: In series opposing configuration, resultant EMF is the difference between individual EMFs.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, the terminals of the ______ should be connected together. [2026]
e: In parallel connection, terminals with the same polarity must be connected together.

q: In a series aiding connection of two or more batteries, the resultant emf will: [2026]
a: remain the same as a single battery
e: Series aiding connection sums up individual EMFs to increase overall voltage.

q: The heating effect of electric current is applied in all of the following appliances EXCEPT: [2026]
e: Refrigerators operate on a cooling compressor cycle, not the heating effect of current.
